marks.gloss_en: שנאמר והיה אם שמוע תשמע -- one who listens will listen [more]: the full vessel holds
דבר אחר: אם שמוע בישן תשמע בחדש
but the way of the Holy One: a full one holds, an empty one does not
R' Yochanan: the etrog on the seventh [day] is forbidden
דאמר רבי זירא: אתרוג שנפסלה אסור לאוכלה כל שבעה -- it remains set aside through all seven
Levi: the etrog is forbidden even on the eighth
איתיביה ריש לקיש לרבי יוחנן: מיד תינוקות שומטין את לולביהן ואוכלין אתרוגיהן -- מאי לאו הוא הדין לגדולים? the same should hold for adults' etrogim, so the etrog is permitted on the seventh
לא, תינוקות דוקא (= p_tinokot_davka)
the mishna: immediately [after the mitzva] children remove their lulavim and eat their etrogim
איכא דאמרי, איתיביה רבי יוחנן לריש לקיש: מיד התינוקות שומטין... תינוקות -- אין, גדולים -- לא! (in this version R' Yochanan objects)
הוא הדין דאפילו גדולים, והאי דקתני תינוקות -- אורחא דמילתא קתני (Reish Lakish's answer in this version; = p_orcha_dmilta)
the same holds even for adults; the mishna says 'children' because it states the usual case
אמר ליה רב פפא לאביי: לרבי יוחנן, מאי שנא סוכה, מאי שנא אתרוג? why is the sukkah forbidden on the eighth while the etrog is permitted?
the sukkah is fit at twilight and so set aside for it and, מיגו, for the whole eighth; the etrog is not fit at twilight (= p_abaye_sukkah_bein_hashmashot, p_abaye_etrog_lo_chazi)

Abaye: the sukkah is fit for use at twilight (should a meal come his way he must sit and eat in it), so it is set aside for twilight, and since it is set aside for twilight it is set aside for the whole eighth day
והלכתא כאביי
in Sura they acted as Mareimar
the stam: they dispute how far the etrog was set aside -- for its mitzva, or for the whole day
R' Zeira: a person should not give a child ownership of the hoshana on the first Festival day
R' Zeira: a person should not tell a child 'I will give you something' and then not give it
the stam: Rav and Rav Asi dispute in the dispute of R' Yochanan and Reish Lakish -- the extent to which the etrog was set aside
Abaye: on the eighth that may be the seventh, [the etrog] is forbidden
Rav: the eighth that may be the seventh counts as the seventh for the sukkah
